parsed.explanation: The combined regime is a protective national framework (gender-identity anti-discrimination law, 2016 legal gender change, transphobia as aggravating factor, conversion-therapy ban, marriage equality) applying to a socially conservative island with thin local recourse. No trans-specific criminalisation or border exclusion is documented. The principal exposure is custody: ID-marker placement puts trans detainees in all-male facilities where they are threatened, and the state watchdog found persisting serious violations across all places of deprivation since 2010 — an unremedied institutional exposure, though conditional on arrest. National combined homophobic/transphobic attacks rose in 2019; no island rate exists. Care waits and a pending under-18 transition ban add friction, not severe harm.

entry_documents.exposure: No island-specific border or document-friction rule is documented; mismatched markers could prompt ordinary secondary questioning, but no gender-marker entry restriction appears.
entry_documents.protection: Home-country documents govern; national law bans gender-identity discrimination and recognises foreign legal gender change. No documented screening, registration or marker-disclosure regime for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: A document/appearance mismatch that escalates into a stop could feed into the custody pipeline where placement rules apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Criminal procedure places detainees by identity-document gender; in practice trans women end up in all-male facilities where other detainees threaten them. The state watchdog found persisting serious violations of trans detainees' rights across all places of deprivation since 2010, extended to the island's jails.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Watchdog oversight exists and issues opinions; transphobia is an aggravating factor for crimes. No evidence these findings have remedied conditions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor stopped over a document mismatch could enter this custody system with no local lawyer and mainland-only inspection record.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The parent state's criminal procedure code governs island jails; placement by document marker routinely yields male-facility placement with documented threats — a state-imposed tier-1 style exposure inside custody.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National legal framework, hate-crime aggravation and watchdog jurisdiction formally extend to the island.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local tolerance does not offset the enforced national custody rule; island inspections have never been documented.

care_services.exposure: 2022 regional report found lack of self-determination, long waits and inequitable access by location; pending senate-passed under-18 transition ban (unresolved since July 2024) could affect a travelling minor.
care_services.protection: Gender care funded by national health insurance; surgery legal since 1979; 2024 national paediatric endocrinology guidelines support puberty blockers; informed-consent reform recommended.
care_services.interaction: A minor seeking care could encounter both island waiting times and an unresolved legislative ban depending on timing.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No documented police targeting of trans people on the island. National police recorded roughly 1,870 homophobic/transphobic attack victims in 2019, up from 1,380 in 2018 — combined, national, dated figures.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Penal code covers gender identity; transphobia an aggravating factor since 2017; conversion therapy banned (2022); hate-crime provisions cover insult, threats and incitement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal protections exist but island-level enforcement of the aggravating factor is undocumented.

minors_guardians.exposure: A same-sex couple's marriage required a 'long and complicated path' on this predominantly Muslim island — one town, one case. A pending under-18 medical transition ban could restrict a minor's care.
minors_guardians.protection: Same-sex marriage legal since 1975; national equality law applies; paediatric endocrinology guidelines support blockers.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's legal status is secure on paper but may meet social friction in local administration.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No island-specific violence data exists. National trend shows rising homophobic/transphobic attacks through 2019; the island's social environment is described as conservative with formal law not equal to lived experience.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime aggravation and discrimination prohibitions supply real recourse; no documented pattern of police failure against trans victims on the island.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of island incident data means neither elevated nor absent risk can be proven — an open question, not safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No LGBT-friendly lawyer is referenced for the island's towns; only a mainland practitioner is listed. No island-specific enforcement record for anti-discrimination or aggravating-factor provisions, and no island detention inspection data.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Full national legal framework, watchdog jurisdiction, working courts and hate-crime remedies formally available via the mainland.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but require travel and delay, weakening practical redress for a short-stay visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: no entry register, no discretionary exclusion, no unappealable exclusion regime. The island's visitor-facing harms are conditional (custody only after arrest) rather than a universal inescapable bar applied at every crossing.

Higher than 0.55-B: no discretionary secondary-screening or refused-admission regime is documented against trans visitors here; equality law and hate-crime provisions supply stronger remedies than a rarely revised appeal desk. Custody exposure is real but not routine at entry.

Slightly below 0.75-C: that anchor shows brief detention ending in release with counsel, compensation and trained officers. Here the watchdog documents persisting serious violations in all places of deprivation with no shown remediation, plus no local lawyer — a heavier custody and recourse deficit.

Comparable to 0.65-A: both combine an official overreach or mistreatment episode with functioning national equality law, intervention and remedies that produce apologies or relief but little discipline — uneven enforcement against solid formal protection.

parsed.synthesis: Law and society diverge. The visitor inherits a strong national framework — gender-identity anti-discrimination, simplified legal gender change, transphobia as an aggravating factor, conversion-therapy ban, marriage equality — with no documented entry, facility or expression restriction, so everyday exposure is modest. Two features pull the score below the low-risk band: an unremedied custody regime that places trans detainees, by document marker, into all-male facilities with documented threats and a watchdog's repeated finding of serious violations across all places of deprivation; and thin island-level recourse (no referenced local lawyer, no island enforcement or inspection data). Social conservatism produces friction, not documented hostility toward visitors. For a travelling minor, the unresolved under-18 transition ban adds care uncertainty. No criminalisation, no state-directed targeting of visitors.
